correctness.rationale: The carry/parity pair after a prefix of length L with value p is (floor((c+p)/2^L), t((c+p) mod 2^L)), so a continuation of value x sees precisely the claimed shifted/complemented residual. If distinct positive translations gave equal or complementary tails, Thue–Morse would have an eventual period; repeatedly halving an even period and applying the recursions to an odd period makes the tail constant, which is impossible. The reachability intervals at quotient q and overflow q+1 have exactly the stated parity counts. For c>=4 there are six low-quotient states including the exceptional split recovery of the quotient-two states at c=5. All high quotients from distinct positive lengths are disjoint since q_j >= 2q_{j+1} > q_{j+1}+1 whenever both layers can contribute high quotients. The initial state is distinct. The four small shifts give 2,3,5,6. Equality in the block bounds for k>=3 is forced at the top digit layer for the minimum, and at every layer from j=2 onward for the maximum. The latter conditions are equivalent to upper-half membership and c=2 mod 4; there are 2^(k-3) such shifts. The binary 2-kernel is exactly the collection of prefix residuals. Independent finite replay (`python3 /workspace/audit-evidence/replay.py 1`) obtained the expected residual signature counts for shifts 0–127 and the stated extremizer sets in blocks k=3–6; this corroborates the proof, not a substitute for it.
residual_risks: No claim for MSD-first automata or for other bases; finite signature bounds alone do not prove the all-shift result.
